doc.title: Low flow in Germany 1992–2025
hero.sub: An area-weighted index built from … gauges of the NIWIS network (the low-flow information system run by Germany's Federal Institute of Hydrology) shows: low-flow spells begin earlier, last longer, and reach larger parts of the river network. The typical year of the past decade has shifted fundamentally.
hero.tile.median.text: Low-flow days in the typical year (median per station and year), from the first to the last decade. The three decades in detail: .
hero.tile.trend.text: of the gauges analysed show a significantly rising trend in low-flow days (Mann-Kendall, p < 0.05)
hero.tile.flaeche.text: Catchment area of the core network ( non-nested gauges; NIWIS, federal and state authorities), of which … lies outside Germany (Alpine Rhine, Moselle, Vltava, upper Oder, among others)
heatmap.lede:
Each cell is one day: the colour shows what share of the gauge network
  was below its local low-flow threshold (Q95 of the reference period) on that day.
  Rows are water years (November–October), 1992 at the top, 2025 at the bottom.
heatmap.aria.basis: Heatmap: share of the gauge network below Q95 per day (Nov–Oct) and water year {von} to {bis}. Peak {spitze} percent on {tag} in water year {jahr}. The most recent decade shows markedly more and longer spells with intense colouring. Use the arrow keys to move through the water years; Enter highlights one in the time series.
heatmap.aria.zusammenfassung: Summary of the heatmap: low-flow spells begin earlier in the more recent water years, last longer, and affect a larger part of the network. Peak: {spitze}% of the network below Q95 on {tag} in water year {jahr}.
heatmap.jahrtip.tasten: ↑ ↓ changes the year, Enter highlights it in the time series
heatmap.jahraria: Water year {jahr}: peak {spitze} percent of the network below Q95 on {tag}, annual mean {mittel} percent{zusatz}.
heatmap.legende.titel: Share of the network below Q95:
heatmap.legende.hinweis:
Clicking a row highlights that year in the time series
      (keyboard: arrow keys ↑ ↓, then Enter)
heatmap.netzhinweis: Network size per day: {min}–{max} reporting gauges (of {gesamt} in the core network). The share shown refers to the gauges reporting on that day.
heatmap.readaid.beginn: Earlier onsetIn the more recent rows the colouring starts as early as high summer, not only in late summer.
heatmap.readaid.dauer: Longer durationThe strongly coloured bands increasingly extend into autumn and winter.
heatmap.readaid.flaeche: Larger extentThe colouring grows more intense: a larger part of the network is affected at the same time.
heatmap.relevanz.text:
When flows stay low for long stretches, inland vessels can only sail with reduced
    draught and therefore less cargo; power plants and industrial sites that use
    river water for cooling or as process water have to throttle back.
    In warm, shallow waters the oxygen content drops: stress for fish and
    small aquatic life. At the same time, agriculture, drinking-water supply
    and industry compete more sharply for abstractions. This analysis measures discharge, not damage.
    It shows how much more frequent and more widespread such situations have become since the
    1990s.
index.lede1: “National” here means: the NIWIS network. Not a single station comes from the state networks of Lower Saxony, Bremen and Hamburg; the north-west is represented only by the federal gauges on the Weser, Aller and Ems. On top of that, the catchments of the major rivers reach far beyond Germany's borders. The index describes the network, not the national territory.
index.lede2:
Area-weighted mean across the gauge network, per water year. Switchable
  by network variant and metric. What the current selection means is stated directly below the controls.
index.variante.primaer.label: Primary (all non-nested gauges)
index.variante.primaer.erklaerung: Primary: all gauges of the core network whose catchment is not already contained in another analysed gauge further downstream. This prevents any area being counted twice (192–208 gauges per year).
index.variante.naturnah.label: Near-natural
index.variante.naturnah.erklaerung: Near-natural: subset of the primary network without dominant human control: no large reservoirs upstream, no water transfers, no mining influence (roughly 100–107 gauges per year, about 14% of the primary network's area).
index.kennzahl.tage.label: Low-flow days (area-weighted)
index.kennzahl.tage.erklaerung: Low-flow days: the number of days in the year on which less water flowed than on 95% of all days in the reference period 1992–2011 (Q95 threshold).
index.kennzahl.defizit.label: Deficit volume (area-weighted)
index.kennzahl.defizit.erklaerung: Flow deficit: how much water was missing in total to hold the threshold; converted to the catchment area (mm of water column) so that large and small rivers are comparable.
index.kennzahl.ssi.label: Standardized Streamflow Index
index.kennzahl.ssi.erklaerung: SSI: standardised drought index: 0 = a normal year, negative = drier than usual, −2 ≈ extremely dry; makes the Rhine and a small upland stream comparable.
index.mk.titel: Trend test (not drawn in the chart)
index.mk.pwert.info: The probability of seeing a pattern this clear purely by chance; below 0.05 the trend counts as statistically significant.
index.mk.sen.info: Robust average change per year, insensitive to outliers.
index.mk.note: {variante}. A trend line would be suggestive given this year-to-year scatter. The test runs on the data, not on the picture.
index.auswahl.hinweis: Highlighted: water year {jahr} (by clicking in the heatmap or on a bar) – {button}
dekaden.lede: Distribution of low-flow days across all station-years, by decade. It is not only the extremes that are rising: the median moves from … days.
dekaden.hinweis: Areas: share of station-years with at least one low-flow day, per 10-day bin; the separated bar on the right collects everything above 200 days (overflow). Vertical dashed line: median of the decade.
dekaden.svg.aria: Distribution of low-flow days by decade
dekaden.achse.x: Low-flow days per station and year
dekaden.nulljahre: {anteile} of station-years per decade had no low-flow day at all. These are not part of the areas.
karte.lede:
Each dot is one gauge; the colour shows the trend in low-flow days
  (Mann-Kendall, 1992–2025), the dot size the magnitude of change (Sen's slope).
  Base map: outline of Germany, federal states and major river courses (Natural Earth);
  the gauges sit on their rivers.
karte.suche.label: Search gauges
karte.a11y.hinweis:
The map is an overview graphic; its dots are deliberately not
    individual tab stops. Every gauge can be reached by keyboard through the “Search gauges” field above
    the map. The detail view below the map shows the same information as the
    map tooltip, plus NM7Q trend, catchment and the year with the highest value.
station.trend.steigend: Low-flow days are increasing: +{sen} days/year, statistically significant ({pwert}).
station.trend.fallend: Low-flow days are decreasing: {sen} days/year, statistically significant ({pwert}).
station.trend.keiner: No statistically significant trend in low-flow days ({pwert}).
station.nm7q.titel: NM7Q = lowest 7-day mean discharge of the year
station.nm7q.label: NM7Q trend
station.fdr.label: After multiple-testing correction
station.fdr.info: Corrects for the fact that {anzahl} gauges are tested at the same time: with that many tests, some gauges would look striking purely by chance. The procedure (Benjamini-Hochberg) raises the p-values accordingly; below 0.05 the trend counts as significant even after the correction.
station.detail.minjahr: Lowest 7-day discharge (NM7Q) of the series in water year {jahr}.
station.detail.sparkcap: Low-flow days per water year; highlighted: the maximum. The trend is given as text on the left.
station.spark.aria: Low-flow days per water year {von} to {bis} for {station}. Maximum: {max} days in water year {maxjahr}.
methodik.daten.text: Daily discharge data from the low-flow information system NIWIS (Federal Institute of Hydrology / LAWA), collected by the responsible federal and state authorities. Per station, the data are subject to the licence terms of the collecting authority (mostly Datenlizenz Deutschland or state licences); this page shows only derived, aggregated metrics. Window: water years 1992–2025 (n = 34). Water year 1991 is incomplete and is therefore left out: NIWIS data begin on 1 January 1991, but the water year starts on 1 November 1990. Its first two months are missing, giving it 304 days instead of 365. Base map of the station map: Natural Earth, 1:10m (public domain), simplified to display scale.
methodik.schwellenwert.text: Low-flow day = daily discharge below the station's own Q95 of the fixed reference period 1992–2011. Metrics per station and water year: number of days below Q95, deficit volume (normalised to catchment area, mm) and Standardized Streamflow Index (SSI). Missing-value sentinels (−777) in the raw data are treated as gaps.
methodik.gewichtung.text:
The national index weights stations by their incremental
    catchment area. Of 191 sink stations, 152 are classified as “nested”
    (area already contained in the basin outlet) and are excluded from the
    authoritative primary variant to avoid double counting (~9% of the
    topology area). A sensitivity run with all stations
    changes neither the direction nor the significance of the trends.
methodik.national.text: The weighted area is larger than Germany: depending on the water year, – to – km² of catchment contribute to the weighting (Germany measures roughly 357,600 km²), because the gauge chains on the Rhine, Elbe, Oder and Danube bring the complete headwaters of their rivers with them. For the five basin outlets it is documented that – km² of that (–% of the maximum weighting mass) lie outside Germany: in Switzerland, Austria, France, Luxembourg, Czechia and above all Poland. The Alpine tributaries Inn and Salzach lie outside these five chains and come on top of that. Counting them in, it is at least roughly 229,000 km² and thus about 45% of the maximum weighting mass. Conversely, the NIWIS network is missing the state networks of Lower Saxony, Bremen and Hamburg entirely: the whole north-west is represented only by federal gauges on the Weser, Aller and Ems, its tributaries (Leine, Hunte, Oste, Ilmenau) not at all. “National” here therefore means the measuring network, not the national territory. Derivation and sources of the area shares: docs/recherche-auslandsanteil.md.
methodik.trendtest.text:
Trend-free prewhitening Mann-Kendall with Sen's slope, per station and for the
    national indices. All four aggregation variants (primary/near-natural, with/without
    nested stations) show the same picture: days and deficit rising
    significantly, SSI falling significantly (all p < 0.05). Robust against the
    reference period (WMO 1991–2020) and event pooling (3/5/7 days).
methodik.multiplizitaet.text: Anyone testing – gauges individually will find some “striking” gauges purely by chance: at a 5% threshold, one in twenty on average. That is why we additionally compute a correction (Benjamini-Hochberg, false discovery rate 5%) that accounts for all gauges being tested at the same time. Of the – gauges with significantly rising low-flow days, – remain significant after this correction; for the lowest 7-day discharge (NM7Q) the number of significantly falling gauges drops from – to –. The picture therefore holds; the correction only makes it more cautious. In the station detail view, the corrected value is shown for each individual station.
methodik.extremwerte.text: A non-stationary GEV fit to the national deficit finds no statistically significant trend in extreme behaviour (likelihood-ratio test p ≈ 0.23). With n = 34 this is a power problem, not evidence of stationarity. The shape parameter is unstable at this sample size; return-period estimates for 2018 vary between 12 and 35 years depending on the parametrisation and are deliberately not reported here as a single figure. The only robust statement is the distribution-free one: 2018 had the highest deficit of a 35-year series.
methodik.grenzen.text:
The near-natural subset covers only ~13–16% of the area of the primary variant
    and is geographically selective. It provides supporting evidence for the direction,
    not a “truer” trend. Homogeneity flags (reservoirs, transfers, mining)
    rest on documented but not exhaustive research. The series only begins
    in 1992; a longer preceding period was not included. The analysis shows
    robust trends, but no attribution of causes (climate, land use, water use).
methodik.repro.text:
All figures on this page come unchanged from this project's analysis pipeline
    (out/national_index.csv, out/station_trends.csv, out/sensitivity.csv,
    data/interim/trend/). Method in detail: methods.md; results documentation:
    docs/ergebnisse-phase4.md. The references are file paths in the public repository.
fuss.quelle: · Data source: NIWIS, operated by the Federal Institute of Hydrology (BfG) and the Länderarbeitsgemeinschaft Wasser (LAWA); data licences per station held by the collecting authorities.
